articles.title: Sport England Objects to Sports Hub Plans in Middleton
articles.excerpt: Sport England has objected to plans for a football and community sports hub on playing fields in Middleton, citing concerns over the loss of current use. The proposed hub, to be located at Bowlee Playing Fields, would feature a training pitch for Rochdale AFC, a 3G pitch, and grass pitches for community use. Sport England, the body responsible for…
articles.content_html:
Sport England has objected to plans for a football and community sports hub on playing fields in Middleton, citing concerns over the loss of current use. The proposed hub, to be located at Bowlee Playing Fields, would feature a training pitch for Rochdale AFC, a 3G pitch, and grass pitches for community use.

Sport England, the body responsible for developing grass-roots sport, has stated that the proposal must meet one of its five exception criteria in order to gain support. In its written response to the planning application, Sport England noted that the proposal would affect the delivery of both football and cricket at the site and that there are outstanding issues that need to be resolved in order for the plans to comply with the exception criteria.

The plans, which are a joint effort between Rochdale Council and Rochdale AFC, aim to create a state-of-the-art sports facility that would benefit the local community. However, Sport England's objections highlight the need for the plans to be revised to address concerns over the impact on the current playing fields. The decision on the planning application is still pending, and it is likely that the plans will be revised to address Sport England's concerns.

The proposed sports hub would include a training pitch for Rochdale AFC, a 3G pitch, and grass pitches for community use, as well as cricket provision, a children's playground, and free parking. Aerial views of the proposed Football and Community Wellbeing Hub at Bowlee Playing Fields in Middleton show Rochdale AFC’s hub in the foreground and the community pitches in the background. The plans have been met with objections from Sport England, who have raised concerns about the proposed Rochdale AFC pavilion’s community changing rooms.

articles.content_html:
The Rochdale board of directors has issued a message to supporters after a disappointing start to their first season back in the EFL. The team has lost four of their opening five league fixtures under Ian Watson, who replaced Jimmy McNulty before the 2026/27 season began.

Ian Watson was appointed after leaving South Shields, who finished 2nd in the National League North. Ahead of a Fans Forum scheduled to take place tomorrow night, the board has indicated they will give Watson more time.

The board's decision comes as the team prepares for their next fixture, with supporters expressing growing unrest at the club's performance. The Fans Forum will provide an opportunity for supporters to ask questions and express their concerns.

The message from the board of directors is likely to be discussed at the Fans Forum. Supporters will be looking for reassurance and a clear plan for improvement.

articles.title: Middleton Regeneration Plans Unveiled at Arena Event
articles.excerpt: Middleton is set to undergo significant regeneration, with plans to bring Metrolink trams to the town and create new homes on brownfield plots.
articles.content_html:
A public event was held at Middleton Arena on September 7, where Greater Manchester's new mayor, Bev Craig, outlined her vision for Middleton's future. The event, attended by around 200 locals, aimed to showcase the town's regeneration plans. Craig was joined on stage by actor and comedian Steve Coogan, CEO of Co-operatives UK Rose Marley, and Rochdale council leader Neil Emmott.

The Middleton Mayoral Development Corporation (MDC) was discussed at the event. The MDC plans to bring Metrolink trams to Middleton, create new homes on brownfield plots, and build high-quality business premises. Additionally, the corporation aims to improve public areas, roads, and pathways in the town. Craig stated that the regeneration plans are about doing things in a collective way, listening to what locals want, and delivering on those promises.

The 'Our Town, Our Future' project, which engaged with over 2,000 residents, found that locals want to see less antisocial behaviour, more shops on the high street, and visible investment in the town. Around a third of respondents expressed a desire to see Warwick Mill brought back into use. Craig pledged her support for the regeneration efforts, saying that the signs of regeneration won't be reduced to a single symbol, but rather will focus on addressing the concerns of Middleton residents.

The MDC plans to address the concerns of locals and deliver a brighter future for Middleton. With Craig's backing, the corporation will work to bring about positive change in the town. The event marked an important step in the regeneration process, as locals and officials came together to discuss the town's future.

articles.content_html:
Ofsted has published a new inspection report for Kids Planet Hopwood, a provider in Rochdale. The report, which was published on 9 September 2026, sets out the findings of the inspection and any rating awarded.

Settings registered on the Early Years Register, such as Kids Planet Hopwood, are normally inspected at least once within a 4-year window. Ofsted prioritises inspections and/or inspects more frequently if concerns are raised. Newly registered settings are inspected within 18 months of the date of their registration.

The inspection report for Kids Planet Hopwood is available to read on the Ofsted website. The website also allows users to search and compare other pre-school, day nursery, and out-of-school care providers in the area. Users can subscribe to alerts to be notified when a new report is published for a specific provider.

For more information about the inspection report or to find other providers in the area, visit the Ofsted website. The website also includes information on how to contact Ofsted with questions or to request a QR code for a printed handout.
